gap: No result ChatGPT got says that a dual extender with no driver needs a separate DisplayPort video stream from the laptop for each added screen, or that clip-on extenders run with the lid open. Apple's own specs give the lid-open count: the base M1 and M3 MacBook Air drive one external display with the lid open (the M3 drives a second only with the lid closed), while the M4 MacBook Air drives two external displays with its built-in screen on. So a driver-free two-screen extender gives you both extra screens on an M4/M5 or Pro/Max Mac, but only one on a base M1, M2 or M3 Mac.
standout_why: I read deskgearhq.com (2026-07-26). It says every pick runs over one USB-C cable using DisplayPort Alt Mode with 'zero driver install' and never mentions Mac external-display limits, lid position, DisplayLink or MST. I also read theofficejournal.com (2026-07-31). It warns that DisplayPort Alt Mode 'isn't universal across every USB-C port' but gives no number of video ports needed and never mentions Mac limits, the lid, DisplayLink or MST. Plugable's USBC-MSTH2 product page, which ChatGPT cited, returned HTTP 429 when I tried it, so I could not read it. Plugable's own help article for that adapter says Macs mirror over MST, so that cited page likely covers the MST-mirroring part. ChatGPT's answer already said that base M1/M2/M3 Macs are 'generally limited to one' external display. No rival page I opened gives Apple's lid-open versus lid-closed numbers per chip, or says that an M4/M5 base Mac drives two screens natively. I could not open gradedpicks.com (TLS error), the FOPO S11 and TUTT S10 pages (HTTP 429), or the Best Buy UPERFECT listing (timeout), so I have not checked those against this finding.
decides: It splits the pick by laptop. On a Windows laptop with two USB-C ports that carry DisplayPort, or on an M4/M5, Pro or Max MacBook, a dual extender connected with one cable per screen works without a driver, so the Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro and the FOPO S7, S11 and S1 dual models are candidates (their own connection paths still need checking). On a base M1, M2 or M3 MacBook, or a MacBook Neo, only one added screen runs natively with the lid open. A single-screen extender such as the Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS, using one USB-C cable with DisplayPort Alt Mode, is then the honest driver-free pick. For a second screen on those Macs you need a driver (Mobile Pixels' software or DisplayLink), and an MST splitter only mirrors on macOS. The FOPO S788 needs FOPO's UsbDisplay driver according to our record, so it fails the question's no-driver terms.

findings.label: Video path for its two screens
findings.value: Two USB-C cables, one per screen. No driver needed if the laptop has two USB-C ports that carry DisplayPort. Base M1/M2 Macs and the MacBook Neo need Mobile Pixels' free driver software.
